svg.title: What the water took, in acres
svg.desc: Rodman pool, flooded (1968): about 13,000 acres; Ground water lowered, Inglis reach (1971): about 9,600 acres; Hardwoods left standing to drown: about 1,135 acres; One property's land taken for the pool (Boynton): about 540 acres. The Inglis figure is 15 square miles, converted.
svg.text: What the water took, in acres
Areas named in the sources of this module. Each label links to its passage.

a.text: One property's land taken for the pool (Boynton)

svg.text: Ground water lowered 0.5 to nearly 15 feet in a 15-square-mile area around the canal below Inglis Lock (USGS, 1973).
How many families lived or farmed on these acres is not counted in the sources read.
